# The discipline

> **Question:** what makes physical AI an engineering discipline of its own, and
> not machine learning with a motor attached?

## Coupling is the dividing line

A physical AI system is coupled to the world in a closed loop. It senses, it
decides, it acts, and the action changes the very world it will sense next. A
cloud model answers a question and forgets it. A physical AI system lives in the
consequences of its own outputs, in real time, under embodied limits, usually
around people. That coupling is the discipline, not the neural network inside it.

## The governing reality

Every engineering discipline answers to an unforgiving reality. For machine
learning systems it is physical law: bandwidth, arithmetic intensity, energy.
For physical AI it is the coupling itself, which imposes four facts that no
amount of model quality removes:

- The world does not pause. Late is wrong, not merely slow.
- Actions have consequences. A mistake moves something, or someone.
- Sensing is partial and noisy. The map is never the territory.
- The device is bounded, and it lives in someone's space.

## Properties before parts

From those facts fall the elements of the discipline: the cross-cutting
properties every system must satisfy, listed and mapped in
[The elements](the-elements.qmd). They are not a final deployment step. They
recur in every component, because the coupling is present in every component.

## The recurring decision: placement

There is one decision the discipline makes over and over. For each capability,
which loop does it run in (reflex, deliberation, learning), and which box
(device, local server, cloud)? Every such choice trades the properties against
one another under a latency, energy, and privacy budget. Learning to make and
defend those choices, with numbers, is the skill this book teaches.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Teaching note"}

- **Hook**: run one task three ways (on the device, on a laptop, in the cloud)
  and let the same task expose a different property each time.
- **Open question**: does this chapter come before or after a first hands-on
  loop? Argument for after: students believe the properties once they have felt
  one.

:::
